nodes.title: Rate limit for read-capability-by-identity
nodes.summary: The read-capability-by-identity route now refuses a source IP's 61st request within a one-minute window with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After value, through an onRequest hook scoped to that route's own plugin registration alone.

nodes.title: Capability-by-identity not-found relocated into a service-level wrapper
nodes.summary: read-capability-by-identity's controller no longer performs its own held-check-and-throw; CapabilityRegistryService now offers a wrapper method it alone calls, while the raw readCapabilityByIdentity and every other consumer of it are unchanged.

nodes.title: Connector-configuration not-found relocated into a service-level wrapper
nodes.summary: read-connector-configuration.controller.ts no longer performs its own held-check-and-throw; ConnectorConfigurationRegistryService.readConnectorConfigurationOrThrow raises ConnectorConfigurationNotFoundError instead, wired only into that route, while the raw readConnectorConfiguration method and every other consumer stay untouched.

nodes.title: Rate limit on the capability-by-identity read route
nodes.summary: Seven Vitest tests, exercised through app.inject() against a real Fastify instance registering createReadCapabilityByIdentityRoutesPlugin(), prove the 61st-request refusal, its Retry-After header, the 60th-and-under pass-through, per-source-IP independence, the hook's confinement to this one route, the window's reset at its boundary, and the one-second Retry-After floor.

nodes.title: Capability-by-identity not-found relocation into a service-level wrapper
nodes.summary: Proves the not-found refusal now originates from CapabilityRegistryService.readCapabilityByIdentityOrThrow rather than the controller, that the controller's handler is now a trivial pass-through, and that the raw readCapabilityByIdentity and test-connector's own refusal are unaffected.

nodes.title: Connector-configuration not-found relocation — service wrapper and controller delegation
nodes.summary: Proves ConnectorConfigurationRegistryService.readConnectorConfigurationOrThrow's two branches and that handleReadConnectorConfigurationRequest performs no held-check-and-throw of its own, delegating entirely to that wrapper.

nodes.title: connector-capability-detail-editing-corrections-backend, first review
nodes.summary: What four passes found over the backend corrective change's three tasks: the not-found relocations for capability and connector-configuration reads, and the capability-identity read's rate limit.
unproven: A request to read-capability-by-identity for a name/version nothing has registered still responds HTTP 404 with CapabilityIdentityNotFoundError, unchanged in condition and message from before the relocation.
No route other than read-capability-by-identity is registered against the rate-limit mechanism this task adds, and every other existing route's tests continue to pass unmodified.

read-capability-by-identity.controller.ts's handleReadCapabilityByIdentityRequest contains no held-check-and-throw of its own; it obtains the refusal, or the resolved capability, from a service-level wrapper method instead.

read-connector-configuration.controller.ts's handleReadConnectorConfigurationRequest contains no held-check-and-throw of its own; it obtains the refusal, or the resolved configuration, from a service-level wrapper method instead.

test-connector.controller.ts's resolveTestedConnectorConfiguration still throws its own ConnectorConfigurationNotFoundError from within test-connector.controller.ts's own code on the same miss, without going through the new wrapper, unaffected by the relocation.
